nodes.label: Three Constituent Tables Architecture
nodes.rationale: constituents is a shared global compound dictionary; herb_constituents links herbs to compounds with concentration levels for colored-pill UI; constituent_profiles is a verbatim CSV import with source fidelity. The three are kept separate to preserve external data provenance while enabling cross-herb phytochemical comparison.

nodes.rationale: constituent_profiles is a flat authoritative CSV import (user-provided); herb_constituents is a curated cross-herb phytochemical network researched by Claude. They are independent and must not be copied between each other.

nodes.label: constituent_profiles Preserves External Name Columns Rationale
nodes.norm_label: constituent_profiles preserves external name columns rationale
nodes.rationale: herb_id can be NULL when CSV herb had no match at import time; source name columns preserve external database's original spelling for future reconciliation. herb_id was added post-import in migration 075.

nodes.label: LEAST/GREATEST Pair Ordering Constraint
nodes.rationale: Always store herb1_id = LEAST(id_a, id_b) and herb2_id = GREATEST(id_a, id_b) to guarantee UNIQUE constraint satisfaction regardless of which herb is listed first in the source text.

nodes.label: Companion Migration Pattern for New Herbs in Case Studies
nodes.norm_label: companion migration pattern for new herbs in case studies
nodes.rationale: ensure_herb creates only a bare row; a companion migration (NNN+1) must fully populate the herb per the adding-herb-data-from-books playbook — energetics, constituents, menstruum, all five external source checks.

nodes.label: Case Study Sort Order Ranges (general 10-190, subjective 200-590, objective 600-790)
nodes.norm_label: case study sort order ranges (general 10-190, subjective 200-590, objective 600-790)
nodes.rationale: Sort order ranges are segregated by section type to prevent collisions between general lifestyle notes, SOAP subjective notes, and objective lab values — allows inserting between existing entries without renumbering.

nodes.label: Quiz Question Count Formula (clamp(15 + H*4 + F*1, 20, 50))
nodes.norm_label: quiz question count formula (clamp(15 + h*4 + f*1, 20, 50))
nodes.rationale: Question count scales with herb count (H*4) and named facts (F*1), with a base of 15, clamped to 20-50. Testing more herbs with more questions ensures adequate coverage without overwhelming sparse classes.

nodes.label: supplement_id Pattern (vitamins/minerals as first-class entities)
nodes.rationale: Vitamins and minerals are in the supplements table as first-class entities. Snippets for them use supplement_id instead of herb_id — they must not be skipped as generic supplements.

nodes.label: No Tone Inference Rule
nodes.rationale: No strong constituent-level rules were found for toning/relaxing tone. Tone must be assigned from clinical source data only — no inference permitted.

nodes.label: No Sour or Salty Inference Rule
nodes.norm_label: no sour or salty inference rule
nodes.rationale: Sour (from organic acids) and salty (from minerals) taste inferences are not reliable at the constituent level — traditional sour herbs are better assigned from primary taste source data; mineral content in plant-bound form does not produce reliable salty perception.
